    "ollama": {
        "api_url": "http://localhost:11434/v1",
        "api_key_env": "OLLAMA_API_KEY",
        "llm": "llama3.1",
        "embeddings": "nomic-embed-text",
        "embeddings_dim": 768,
        "documentation": "https://ollama.com/download",
    },
}


def provider_preset(name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Return the preset of a provider (empty dict when unknown).

    Args:
        name: Preset/provider name (``openai``, ``deepseek``, ``custom`` ...).

    Returns:
        The preset dictionary, or an empty dict for an unknown provider.
    """
    return PROVIDER_PRESETS.get((name or "").strip().lower(), {})


def list_provider_presets() -> List[dict]:
    """
    Describe every provider preset, **including the models it will define**.

    This is what an installer or the first-run wizard shows after the user picks
    a provider: the models are not guessed by the caller, they come from the
    preset. No key is ever included.

    Returns:
        One entry per provider with ``name``, ``api_url``, ``api_key_env``,
        ``provider``, ``documentation`` and the ``models`` it configures
        (chat / wiki / embeddings + vector size).
    """
    presets: List[dict] = []
    for name, preset in PROVIDER_PRESETS.items():
        llm = preset.get("llm", "")
        wiki = preset.get("wiki", "") or llm
        embeddings = preset.get("embeddings", "")
        models = [
            {
                "role": "chat",
                "slot": "llm_model",
                "entry": LLM_MODEL_NAME,
                "ai_model": llm,
                "type": AIModelType.llm.value,
            }
        ]
        if wiki and wiki != llm:
            models.append(
                {
                    "role": "wiki",
                    "slot": "wiki_model",
                    "entry": "wiki",
                    "ai_model": wiki,
                    "type": AIModelType.llm.value,
                }
            )
        if embeddings:
            models.append(
                {
                    "role": "embeddings",
                    "slot": "embeddings_model",
                    "entry": EMBEDDINGS_MODEL_NAME,
                    "ai_model": embeddings,
                    "type": AIModelType.embeddings.value,
                    "vector_size": preset.get("embeddings_dim", 0),
                }
            )
        presets.append(
            {
                "name": name,
                "api_url": preset.get("api_url", ""),
                "api_key_env": preset.get("api_key_env", ""),
                "documentation": preset.get("documentation", ""),
                "requires_api_url": name == "custom",
                "knowledge_enabled": bool(embeddings),
                "models": models,
            }
        )
    return presets


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Environment helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _env(name: str, default: str = "") -> str:
    """Read and strip an environment variable, returning ``default`` if empty."""
    return (os.environ.get(name) or default).strip()


def _value(
    config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]], key: str, env_name: str, default: str = ""
) -> str:
    """
    Resolve one setting, letting an explicit configuration win over the env.

    The installer and the first-run wizard send their settings in the request
    body, while a container started with ``-e`` keeps working unchanged because
    the environment is the fallback.

    Args:
        config: Explicit configuration (may be ``None``).
        key: Key inside ``config`` (e.g. ``"provider"``).
        env_name: Environment variable used as fallback.
        default: Value returned when neither is set.

    Returns:
        The stripped value; never ``None``.
    """
    if config:
        value = config.get(key)
        if value is not None and str(value).strip():
            return str(value).strip()
    return _env(env_name, default)


def _detect_provider(config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> str:
    """
    Resolve which provider the caller is asking to configure.

    Priority: explicit configuration, ``CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER``, then the
    first well-known provider whose API key is present, then nothing.
    """
    name = _value(config, "provider", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER").lower()
    if name:
        return name

    for preset_name, preset in PROVIDER_PRESETS.items():
        if preset_name == "ollama":
            continue
        if _env(preset["api_key_env"]):
            logger.info("AI bootstrap: detected provider '%s' from %s", preset_name, preset["api_key_env"])
            return preset_name

    if _env("CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY") or _env("CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL"):
        return "custom"

    return ""


def _resolve_api_key(
    provider: str, preset: dict, config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
) -> str:
    """Resolve the API key: explicit configuration first, then the env."""
    return _value(config, "api_key", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY") or _env(preset.get("api_key_env", ""))


def _resolve_api_url(
    provider: str, preset: dict, config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
) -> str:
    """Resolve the base URL: explicit configuration, then the env, then the preset."""
    return _value(config, "api_url", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL") or preset.get("api_url", "")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Settings builder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_provider_and_models(config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> Optional[dict]:
    """
    Build the provider/models description requested by the caller.

    The models are **derived from the provider preset**: the installer only says
    which provider and key to use, and every role (chat / wiki / embeddings) is
    filled from :data:`PROVIDER_PRESETS`. Any role can still be overridden
    explicitly with ``model``, ``wiki_model`` or ``embeddings_model``.

    Args:
        config: Optional explicit configuration (installer/wizard payload).
                Recognised keys: ``provider``, ``api_key``, ``api_url``,
                ``model``, ``wiki_model``, ``rag_model``, ``guardrail_model``,
                ``embeddings_model``, ``embeddings_dim``, ``context_length``.

    Returns:
        ``None`` when nothing asks for a bootstrap, otherwise a dict with the
        ``provider`` (AIProvider), ``models`` (List[AIModel]), the ``slots`` to
        apply on :class:`GlobalSettings` and a readable ``description``.
    """
    provider_name = _detect_provider(config)
    if not provider_name:
        return None

    preset = provider_preset(provider_name)
    api_url = _resolve_api_url(provider_name, preset, config)
    api_key = _resolve_api_key(provider_name, preset, config)

    if not api_url:
        logger.warning(
            "AI bootstrap: provider '%s' needs CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL (OpenAI-compatible '/v1' endpoint). Skipping.",
            provider_name,
        )
        return None

    if provider_name == "anthropic":
        # Anthropic does not expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: it needs an
        # OpenAI-compatible gateway in front of it.
        logger.warning(
            "AI bootstrap: 'anthropic' has no OpenAI-compatible endpoint. "
            "Run an OpenAI-compatible gateway and set CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL."
        )
        return None

    if not api_key and provider_name != "ollama":
        logger.warning(
            "AI bootstrap: no API key for provider '%s'. Set CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY. Skipping.",
            provider_name,
        )
        return None

    context_length = int(_env("CODX_JUNIOR_AI_CONTEXT_LENGTH", "0") or 0)

    llm_model = _value(config, "model", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL") or preset.get("llm", "")
    if not llm_model:
        logger.warning("AI bootstrap: provider '%s' needs CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL. Skipping.", provider_name)
        return None

    wiki_model = (
        _value(config, "wiki_model", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_WIKI_MODEL")
        or preset.get("wiki", "")
        or llm_model
    )
    rag_model = _value(config, "rag_model", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_RAG_MODEL") or llm_model
    guardrail_model = (
        _value(config, "guardrail_model", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_GUARDRAIL_MODEL") or llm_model
    )
    embeddings_model = _value(
        config, "embeddings_model", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL"
    ) or preset.get("embeddings", "")
    embeddings_dim = int(
        _value(
            config,
            "embeddings_dim",
            "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_EMBEDDINGS_DIM",
            str(preset.get("embeddings_dim", 0)),
        )
        or 0
    )
    context_length = int(_value(config, "context_length", "CODX_JUNIOR_AI_CONTEXT_LENGTH", "0") or 0)

    provider = AIProvider(
        name=provider_name,
        provider=provider_name,
        api_url=api_url,
        api_key=api_key,
        admin_url=preset.get("admin_url", ""),
    )

    models: List[AIModel] = [
        AIModel(
            name=LLM_MODEL_NAME,
            ai_model=llm_model,
            model_type=AIModelType.llm,
            ai_provider=provider_name,
            settings=AILLMModelSettings(context_length=context_length or 0),
        )
    ]

    slots = {
        "llm_model": LLM_MODEL_NAME,
        "rag_model": LLM_MODEL_NAME,
        "wiki_model": LLM_MODEL_NAME,
        "guardrail_model": LLM_MODEL_NAME,
    }

    # Optional: one model entry per role, so the wiki can use a bigger model
    # than the chat without editing the settings from the UI.
    if wiki_model != llm_model:
        models.append(
            AIModel(
                name="wiki",
                ai_model=wiki_model,
                model_type=AIModelType.llm,
                ai_provider=provider_name,
                settings=AILLMModelSettings(context_length=context_length or 0),
            )
        )
        slots["wiki_model"] = "wiki"

    if embeddings_model:
        models.append(
            AIModel(
                name=EMBEDDINGS_MODEL_NAME,
                ai_model=embeddings_model,
                model_type=AIModelType.embeddings,
                ai_provider=provider_name,
                settings=AIEmbeddingModelSettings(vector_size=embeddings_dim or 1536),
            )
        )
        slots["embeddings_model"] = EMBEDDINGS_MODEL_NAME
    else:
        logger.warning(
            "AI bootstrap: provider '%s' has no embeddings model configured: "
            "knowledge/RAG search stays disabled until one is set "
            "(CODX_JUNIOR_AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL).",
            provider_name,
        )

    return {
        "provider": provider,
        "models": models,
        "slots": slots,
        "preset": provider_name if provider_name in PROVIDER_PRESETS else "custom",
        "description": {
            "provider": provider_name,
            "api_url": api_url,
            "llm_model": llm_model,
            "rag_model": rag_model,
            "wiki_model": wiki_model,
            "guardrail_model": guardrail_model,
            "embeddings_model": embeddings_model,
            "embeddings_dim": embeddings_dim,
        },
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Entry points
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def bootstrap_ai_from_env(
    force: bool = False,
    apply: bool = True,
    config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> dict:
    """
    Configure the AI provider/models from the environment or a explicit config.

    Args:
        force: Re-apply even when a provider is already configured.
        apply: When ``False`` only report what would be configured (dry run).
        config: Optional explicit configuration (installer/wizard payload) that
                takes precedence over the environment variables.

    Returns:
        A JSON-serialisable summary, also persisted for ``GET /api/bootstrap``.
    """
    summary: dict = {
        "enabled": _env(ENV_ENABLED, "1") not in ("0", "false", "no"),
        "applied": False,
        "reason": "",
        "provider": "",
        "preset": "",
        "models": [],
        "models_detail": [],
        "slots": {},
    }

    if not summary["enabled"]:
        summary["reason"] = f"{ENV_ENABLED}=0"
        return summary

    # Only the API process writes settings: the background worker shares the
    # same files and running the bootstrap twice would just add noise.
    if _env("CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND"):
        summary["reason"] = "background process"
        return summary

    try:
        from codx.junior.global_settings import (
            read_global_settings,
            write_global_settings,
        )

        settings = read_global_settings()

        already_configured = [
            provider.name
            for provider in settings.ai_providers or []
            if provider.name != DEFAULT_PROVIDER
        ]
        force = force or bool(config) or _env(ENV_FORCE) == "1"

        if already_configured and not force:
            summary["reason"] = f"already configured: {', '.join(already_configured)}"
            summary["provider"] = already_configured[0]
            return summary

        built = build_provider_and_models(config)
        if not built:
            summary["reason"] = "no provider requested in the environment"
            return summary

        provider: AIProvider = built["provider"]
        models: List[AIModel] = built["models"]
        slots: dict = built["slots"]

        summary["provider"] = provider.name
        summary["preset"] = built.get("preset", provider.name)
        summary["models"] = [model.name for model in models]
        summary["models_detail"] = [
            {
                "entry": model.name,
                "ai_model": model.ai_model,
                "type": model.model_type.value,
            }
            for model in models
        ]
        summary["slots"] = slots

        if not apply:
            summary["applied"] = False
            summary["reason"] = "dry run"
            logger.info("AI bootstrap (dry run): %s", json.dumps(built["description"]))
            return summary

        settings.ai_providers = [
            existing for existing in (settings.ai_providers or [])
            if existing.name not in (provider.name, DEFAULT_PROVIDER)
        ] + [provider]

        settings.ai_models = [
            existing for existing in (settings.ai_models or [])
            if existing.ai_provider not in (provider.name, DEFAULT_PROVIDER)
        ] + models

        for slot, value in slots.items():
            setattr(settings, slot, value)

        write_global_settings(settings)

        summary["applied"] = True
        summary["reason"] = "configured from environment"
        logger.info("AI bootstrap applied: %s", json.dumps(built["description"]))
        _write_marker(summary)
        return summary

    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive, never break boot
        logger.exception("AI bootstrap failed: %s", ex)
        summary["reason"] = f"error: {ex}"
        return summary


def _marker_path() -> str:
    """Path of the last bootstrap summary (inside the settings folder)."""
    home = os.environ.get("HOME", "/tmp")
    folder = os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_CONFIG_FOLDER", home)
    return os.path.join(folder, "bootstrap.json")


def _write_marker(summary: dict) -> None:
    """Persist the summary so the UI/tools can report how the demo was configured."""
    try:
        path = _marker_path()
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(summary, handle, indent=2)
    except OSError as ex:
        logger.warning("AI bootstrap: could not write %s: %s", _marker_path(), ex)

Compared to the removed :class:`codx.junior.ai.openai_ai.OpenAI_AI`, this
implementation:
    * exposes a single async ``chat()`` method (no sync variant),
    * uses an **iterative** tool loop instead of recursion,
    * delegates loop protection to :class:`LoopGuard`,
    * delegates logging, event emission and cancellation to

    * keeps streaming, callbacks, cancellation and analytics.
    * caches tool results per conversation to avoid re-execution.
    * returns a typed :class:`AgentRunResult` (no untyped ``additional_kwargs``).
    * decides which profile tools to inject into the request (see
      :meth:`SmolAgent._profile_tools_for_run`): the profile definition itself
      never carries them.

Tool events (``TOOL_START`` / ``TOOL_END`` / ``TOOL_ERROR`` / ``TOOL_LOGS``) carry the
``tool_call_id``, the parsed JSON request args and a truncated result preview
so listeners (e.g. the ChatEventBridge) can surface tool executions as chat
messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's
user-facing ``output`` (see Message Structure below). Tool logs are emitted for
forensic audit trail.

Loop-Limit Handling
When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Tool-Limit Continuation (harness tasks)
The tool limits are a **guardrail**, not a stop condition for harness work. On
a harness turn (orchestration worker, run supervisor, delegated subagent or the
``codx-junior`` harness profile) that reaches a limit, the agent does NOT end
the turn: it injects a "path rethink" notice carrying every fact already
collected (deterministic ledger, no extra AI call) plus the instruction to use
fewer tools, change approach, or ask the user for the exact decision it needs,
and it renews the guard with a smaller budget (``TOOL_LIMIT_CONTINUATIONS``).
The turn only stops when the continuations are exhausted, and that stop is
reported as "needs a human decision" instead of a silent failure. Plain chats
keep the previous behaviour (stop + tool-usage summary).

Cost-Limit Handling
Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it
on the returned :class:`AgentRunResult` (``result.cost``). Tools that report
their own cost through :attr:`ToolResponse.cost` are summed into both the
per-run total and the chat total. The chat total is seeded from ``Chat.cost``
(the accumulated, deletion-safe value maintained by ChatManager) so the budget
applies to the whole chat and is not reset when messages are deleted. When the
chat reaches its estimated cost (``Chat.estimation_cost``), the run stops
gracefully — before executing further tools — to keep the chat within budget.

Message Structure
A single final assistant message is always produced. Its ``content`` holds only
the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final
answer. Tool output is NO LONGER merged into the message content. For
dual-response tools, ``ToolResponse.user_response`` is emitted on the ``TOOL_END``
event and attached to the response message as a collapsible property
(``ToolEvent.output``), so the client decides how to render it (collapsed or
hidden) and the chat stays clean.

Profile tools
Profiles learn per project, so the tools that read/write what a profile has
learned are decided **per run** by this agent:

The profiles participating in the turn are declared by the chat engine in an
internal ``profiles`` request header, which is consumed here and never
forwarded to the provider.

Vision API Support
Binary files (PDFs, images) are passed as vision content when models support it.
The content is merged into the final user message to enable vision-capable models
to process images and documents alongside text.

Error Visibility
Every AI provider interaction (the completion request, the streaming of its
response and the tool-usage summary request) is guarded so failures are logged

Never wrap a file change inside a plain markdown code fence. Propose file changes only as follows.

<file_change/>

 * Use valid file path (absolute or relative) based on the project and conversation context.
 * New file changes must follow original file formating and indentation.
 * Avoid unnecessary changes, format changes, or cleanup unless explicitely been asked for it.
 * Keep changes simple and easy to review by the user.

### TOOL USAGE — do not repeat work
 * Before calling a tool, check the conversation history and the <session_memory>
   block: if the information is already there, use it instead of calling the tool.
 * NEVER repeat an identical tool call (same tool + same arguments) in the same

 * When a large file was already read partially, request ONLY the missing

 * Batch independent queries/files into a single call whenever the tool

 * For a runtime symptom ("not working", "blank", "nothing shows", "not

   / browser console / network request, container or app logs, the failing API
   response. Reading code only confirms a hypothesis; it is not evidence.

   search. The legacy discovery tools are hidden while the atlas is enforced.

   code, tests and docs. Use project_trace to follow a flow instead of reading
   every file on the path.

   use project_read_file with start_line/end_line or pattern="symbol" and do
   not page through the whole file.
 * Work in small loops: after at most 3-5 discovery calls, state a concrete
   hypothesis, run the smallest probe or make the smallest change that tests
   it, then verify. Alternate investigation and action; never spend the whole
   turn reading.
 * Before the tool budget runs out, write down in your answer: what is
   confirmed, what is ruled out, and the single next concrete step. Never end
   a run with only tool calls and no findings.

### PROJECT ATLAS — the canonical way to find resources
 * `project_map(query="", path="")` — orient: domains, entry points, key files,
   reading order. Call it once at the start of a non-trivial task.
 * `project_locate(query, kind=..., include=..., regex=...)` — find: symbols,

 * Never search `.codx` for a code bug, and never search the codebase for a
   task, profile or session. Use the matching namespace.
"""


# Secrets are part of the global system instructions on purpose: a model that
# does not know the handle syntax asks the user for the credential instead, and
# the value ends up in the transcript. See
# ``codx/junior/security/ciso/vault.py`` for the resolver.
SECRETS_SYSTEM_RULES = """
### SECRETS — never ask for, type or print a credential
The runtime holds the credentials; you only NAME them with a handle:

  {{secret:NAME}}   a value stored in the project or the global vault
  {{env:NAME}}      a value already present in the runtime environment

Rules:
 * Never ask the user to paste a credential in a message: it would be stored in
   the transcript, the index and the provider logs. Never print, log, summarise
   or write a resolved value anywhere.
 * Call `secrets_list` to learn which names exist. Never guess a name: an
   unknown handle fails the tool call.
 * A handle is accepted ONLY as the WHOLE value of the `env` map or of the
   `stdin` argument of a command tool. Anywhere else — inside a command string,
   a URL, a file, a description — the call is refused with `denied_sink`,
   because that is exactly how a value escapes.
 * Correct: {"command": "docker login --password-stdin registry.local",
             "stdin": "{{secret:REGISTRY_PASSWORD}}"}
 * Correct: {"command": "aws s3 ls",
             "env": {"AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY": "{{secret:AWS_KEY}}"}}
 * Wrong:   {"command": "docker login -p {{secret:REGISTRY_PASSWORD}} host"}
 * Wrong:   {"url": "https://user:{{secret:TOKEN}}@host/"}
 * The child process expands the value itself (`$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` inside
   the command is plain shell, not a handle). Write the option that reads the
   value from stdin or the environment, never one that takes it as an argument.
 * A missing secret is requested with `secrets_request(name, reason)`. The
   operator provides it out of band and `secrets_list` then reports it `ready`.
 * If a call fails with `denied_tool`, the allow list of that secret does not
   include the tool: report it, do not look for a workaround.
"""


def _build_secrets_instructions(settings: Any = None) -> str:
    """
    Return the secrets block of the system prompt: the rules plus the inventory.

    The inventory is value-free (names, availability and allow list only, see
    :func:`codx.junior.security.ciso.vault.dashboard_entries`) and is read fresh
    on every turn, so a secret added from the settings UI is usable immediately
    without the model calling ``secrets_list`` first.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings, used to locate the vault and the policy.

    Returns:
        The instructions to append, or an empty string when secrets are disabled
        by policy.
    """
    parts: List[str] = []
    try:
        from codx.junior.security.ciso import vault as secret_vault

        if not secret_vault.vault_for(settings).secret_policy.enabled:
            return ""
        entries = secret_vault.dashboard_entries(settings)
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.warning("SmolAgent: could not read the secret inventory: %s", ex)
        entries = None

    parts.append(SECRETS_SYSTEM_RULES)
    if entries is None:
        return "\n".join(parts)

    if not entries:
        parts.append(
            "### SECRETS — available now\n"
            "No secret is declared for this project or globally. Call "
            "`secrets_request(name, reason)` when the task needs one."
        )
        return "\n".join(parts)

    lines = ["### SECRETS — handles available now (names only, never values)"]
    for entry in entries:
        name = str(entry.get("name") or "").strip()
        if not name:
            continue
        allowed = ", ".join(entry.get("allow_tools") or []) or "any tool"
        status = str(entry.get("status") or "ready")
        lines.append(f" * {{{{secret:{name}}}}} — {status}; allowed tools: {allowed}")
    lines.append(
        "Use one only as the WHOLE value of `env.<NAME>` or `stdin`."
    )
    parts.append("\n".join(lines))
    return "\n".join(parts)


def _iso_utc(epoch_seconds: float) -> str:
    """
    Format an epoch timestamp as an ISO-8601 UTC string.

    Used by the timing instrumentation (tool invocations and provider calls),
    where a wall-clock timestamp is needed next to the monotonic duration: the
    clock says *when* it happened (so lines from different components can be
    merged into one time frame) while the duration stays immune to clock jumps.

    Args:
        epoch_seconds: Value from ``time.time()``.

    Returns:
        An ISO-8601 string with millisecond precision and a ``Z`` suffix.
    """
    return datetime.utcfromtimestamp(epoch_seconds).strftime(
        "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f"
    )[:-3] + "Z"


def _env_float(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    """Read a positive float from the environment (fallback on unset/invalid)."""
    raw = os.environ.get(name)
    if raw is None or not str(raw).strip():
        return default
    try:
        value = float(raw)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        logger.warning("SmolAgent: invalid %s=%r, using %.1f", name, raw, default)
        return default
    return value if value > 0 else default


def _env_int(name: str, default: int) -> int:
    """Read a non-negative int from the environment (fallback on unset/invalid)."""
    raw = os.environ.get(name)
    if raw is None or not str(raw).strip():
        return default
    try:
        value = int(raw)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        logger.warning("SmolAgent: invalid %s=%r, using %d", name, raw, default)
        return default
    return value if value >= 0 else default


def _get_analytics() -> Analytics:
    """Return (creating if necessary) the module-level Analytics singleton."""
    global _analytics_instance
    if _analytics_instance is None:
        _analytics_instance = Analytics()
    return _analytics_instance


def _load_chat_global_instructions() -> str:
    """
    Load chat_global_instructions from GlobalSettings.

    This is called on every chat (not cached) to ensure instructions
    are always up-to-date.

    Returns:
        The chat_global_instructions string from GlobalSettings, or empty
        string if not available.
    """
    try:
        from codx.junior.global_settings import read_global_settings
        global_settings = read_global_settings()
        return "\n".join([
            (global_settings.chat_global_instructions or "").strip(),
            HARDCODED_SYSTEM_RULES
        ])
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.warning(
            "SmolAgent: failed to load chat_global_instructions: %s", ex
        )
        return ""


def _normalise_tool_result(result: Any, func_name: str) -> str:
    """
    Convert any tool return value into a non-empty string suitable for an
    OpenAI tool-result message.

    The model MUST always receive a non-empty tool message. An empty, None,
    or missing content causes it to re-issue the exact same tool call,
    producing an infinite loop that only terminates via LoopGuard.

    ENHANCED: Now handles more edge cases where tools might return falsy values:
    - Empty lists/dicts
    - Zero (which is falsy but valid)
    - False boolean (which is falsy but valid)

    Conversion rules (in priority order):
        1. ``None``             → sentinel ``_TOOL_NO_OUTPUT``
        2. ``str``              → returned as-is (empty str → sentinel)
        3. ``dict``/``list``    → JSON-serialised for readability
        4. ``0`` or ``False``   → serialised as string (not sentinel!)
        5. Anything else        → ``str()`` fallback

    Args:
        result:    Raw value returned by the tool callable.
        func_name: Tool name used only for debug logging.

    Returns:
        A non-empty string representation of the result.
    """
    # Handle None explicitly (common case)
    if result is None:
        logger.debug(
            "SmolAgent: tool '%s' returned None – using sentinel '%s'",
            func_name,
            _TOOL_NO_OUTPUT,
        )
        return _TOOL_NO_OUTPUT

    # Handle strings (including empty)
    if isinstance(result, str):
        if not result.strip():
            logger.debug(
                "SmolAgent: tool '%s' returned empty string – using sentinel",
                func_name,
            )
            return _TOOL_NO_OUTPUT
        return result

    # Handle empty lists/dicts (valid return values, not "no output")
    if isinstance(result, (list, dict)):
        if not result:  # Empty list or dict
            logger.debug(
                "SmolAgent: tool '%s' returned empty %s – serialising as JSON",
                func_name,
                type(result).__name__,
            )
            return json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)
        try:
            return json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return str(result)

    # Handle falsy but valid values (0, False, etc.)
    # These SHOULD be serialised, not replaced with sentinel
    if result == 0 or result is False:
        logger.debug(
            "SmolAgent: tool '%s' returned %r (falsy but valid)",
            func_name,
            result,
        )
        return str(result)

    # Fallback: serialize any other type
    try:
        return json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        serialized = str(result)
        # Guard against empty string from str() fallback
        if not serialized.strip():
            logger.warning(
                "SmolAgent: tool '%s' returned %r which str() converted to empty string",
                func_name,
                result,
            )
            return _TOOL_NO_OUTPUT
        return serialized


def _format_ai_error(ex: BaseException) -> str:
    """
    Build a verbose, single-line description of an AI provider error.

    Connection failures against the LLM provider previously reached the logs
    only as ``str(ex)`` (e.g. ``"Connection error."``), which made them
    impossible to diagnose. This helper extracts every diagnostic the
    the OpenAI/httpx clients expose — HTTP status, error code/param, provider
    request id, response body — plus the chained root cause
    (``httpx.ConnectError``, ``socket.gaierror``, ``ReadTimeout``, TLS/proxy
    failures, ...) so the origin of the failure is visible from the log line
    alone.

    Args:
        ex: The exception raised while talking to the AI provider.

    Returns:
        A pipe-separated description of the error, safe for logging.
    """
    parts: List[str] = [f"type={type(ex).__name__}", f"message={ex}"]

    # Provider errors (openai.APIStatusError / APIConnectionError) may carry
    # an HTTP response with status code, headers and body.
    response = getattr(ex, "response", None)
    if response is not None:
        parts.append(f"http_status={getattr(response, 'status_code', '?')}")
        headers = getattr(response, "headers", None) or {}
        provider_request_id = None
        try:
            provider_request_id = (
                headers.get("x-request-id")
                or headers.get("request-id")
            )
        except (AttributeError, TypeError):
            # Defensive: unusual header container — request id is optional.
            provider_request_id = None
        if provider_request_id:
            parts.append(f"provider_request_id={provider_request_id}")
        body = ""
        try:
            body = response.text or ""
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive: unreadable body
            body = ""
        if body:
            parts.append(f"body={body[:AI_ERROR_BODY_MAX_CHARS]}")

    # Attributes exposed directly by the provider client errors.
    for attr in ("code", "param", "status_code", "request_id", "body"):
        value = getattr(ex, attr, None)
        if value is not None:
            parts.append(f"{attr}={value}")

    # The real root cause (DNS, connection refused, timeout, TLS, proxy, ...)
    # is usually chained on the provider error.
    cause = ex.__cause__ or ex.__context__
    if cause is not None:
        parts.append(f"cause={type(cause).__name__}: {cause}")

    return " | ".join(str(part) for part in parts)


class SmolAgent:
    """
    Async-only streaming chat agent with multi-step tool support.

    All logging, event fan-out, cancellation checkpoints and per-run
    analytics are delegated to :class:`AgentRunContext` (the unified
    agent runtime). Callers may pass their own context through
    ``config["run_context"]`` (e.g. to share a Socket.IO listener or a
    cancellation token) or plain listeners via ``config["event_listeners"]``.

    Conversation flow
    ```mermaid
        flowchart TD
            A[chat] --> B[Resolve AgentRunContext]
            B --> C[run_context.run - RUN_START]
            C --> D[Build OpenAI messages]
            D --> E[Initialize ToolCache]
            E --> F[Stream completion via guard_stream]
            F -->|chunk| F1[Accumulate chunk]
            F1 -->|flush| F2[Callback with FULL accumulated content]
            F --> G{finish_reason?}
            G -->|tool_calls| H[Check ToolCache]
            H -->|HIT| H1[Skip _execute_tool - use cached]
            H -->|HIT| H2[Emit TOOL_END with cached=true]
            H -->|HIT - ToolResponse| H3[No output re-emitted - first run delivered it]
            H -->|MISS| I[LoopGuard.check - depth & breadth & stuck]
            I -->|ok| J[Execute tool - TOOL_START/END/ERROR/LOGS + output]
            H1 --> K{Dual-response tool?}
            J --> K
            K -->|yes| K1[user_response - collapsible TOOL_END output property]
            K -->|yes| K2[Send llm_response as tool result to model only]
            K -->|no| K3[Send normalised result as tool result to model only]
            K1 --> L[Append to openai_messages]
            K2 --> L
            K3 --> L
            L --> F
            I -->|limit exceeded| M[Summarise tool usage and finish gracefully]
            G -->|stop / length| N[Append final LLM text to final_answer_content]
            N --> O[Append final AIMessage + return typed AgentRunResult]
            M --> O
            O --> P[Record usage + cache stats - RUN_END]
            F -->|cancelled| Q[RUN_CANCELLED - raise CancelledError]
            F -->|provider error| R[Verbose AI error log + client notice - raise]
    ```
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
        llm_model: Optional[str] = None,
        user: Optional[CodxUser] = None,
        system: Optional[str] = None,
        session: Optional[Any] = None,
        harness: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Args:
            settings:  Project settings providing LLM configuration.
            llm_model: Optional model override.
            user:      Optional user (used for API key and analytics).
            system:    Optional extra system prompt content (appended after
                      chat_global_instructions).
            session:   Optional session context (injected for tools that need
                      access to current chat or session state).
            harness:   When False the run is a PLAIN completion: no agent
                      system prompt and no tool schemas. Use it for
                      single-shot prompts (docs assistant, enrichment) where
                      tool calling would only produce unusable output.
        """
        self.harness: bool = harness
        # Copy the registry: MCP tools are project-scoped and are appended to
        # this instance. Mutating the module-level TOOLS would leak one
        # project's CRM tools into every other project in the process.
        self.tools: List[Dict[str, Any]] = list(TOOLS)

        self.settings = settings
        self.llm_settings = settings.get_llm_settings(llm_model=llm_model)
        self.model: str = self.llm_settings.model
        self.user = user
        self.api_key: str = (
            user.api_key if user and user.api_key else self.llm_settings.api_key
        )
        self.base_url: str = self.llm_settings.api_url
        # Store extra system instructions; global instructions will be loaded
        # dynamically on each chat to ensure freshness
        self.extra_system: str = (system or "").strip()
        # Store session context for tools that need access to it
        self.session: Optional[Any] = session
        # Maximum seconds a single tool may run before it is aborted. A hung
        # tool used to block the whole chat turn (and the event loop) forever.
        # Priority: tool settings > model/provider > env > default.
        self.tool_timeout_seconds: float = self._resolve_tool_timeout_seconds()
        # How many independent tool calls of ONE round may run concurrently.
        # Most tools are I/O bound (file reads, HTTP, git/docker CLI), so a
        # round of independent calls costs the latency of its slowest call
        # instead of the sum. Mutating/session-bound calls are barriers, see
        # codx.junior.ai.smol.parallel. 1 restores sequential execution.
        self.tool_parallelism: int = self._resolve_tool_parallelism()
        # Sticky thinking-mode switch. Thinking-mode providers (DeepSeek) reject
        # a request that carries ``tools`` when the chain of thought of a
        # previous assistant turn is missing. Once the provider rejects the
        # payload for that reason the turn continues WITHOUT thinking mode,
        # so the rejected payload is never re-sent round after round.
        self._thinking_disabled: bool = False

        # Transport limits: the SDK default (10 minutes, 2 retries) turns a
        # half-open connection into a turn that looks stuck forever. The READ
        # timeout is an idle timeout, not a cap on total thinking: DeepSeek may
        # spend a long time before the first token, but it must not stay silent.
        self.llm_timeout = httpx.Timeout(
            connect=_env_float(
                ENV_LLM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
                DEFAULT_LLM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            ),
            read=_env_float(
                ENV_LLM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
                DEFAULT_LLM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            ),
            write=_env_float(
                ENV_LLM_WRITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
                DEFAULT_LLM_WRITE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            ),
            pool=_env_float(
                ENV_LLM_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
                DEFAULT_LLM_POOL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            ),
        )
        self.llm_max_retries: int = _env_int(
            ENV_LLM_MAX_RETRIES, DEFAULT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES
        )
        self.client = OpenAI(
            api_key=self.api_key,
            base_url=self.base_url,
            timeout=self.llm_timeout,
            max_retries=self.llm_max_retries,
        )
        logger.info(
            "SmolAgent created. USER: %s, MODEL: %s, URL: %s, "
            "TOOL_TIMEOUT: %ss, TOOL_PARALLELISM: %d, "
            "LLM_TIMEOUT: connect=%.0fs read=%.0fs write=%.0fs pool=%.0fs "
            "retries=%d (effort limits come from the active profiles)",
            user.username if user else "NONE",
            self.model,
            self.base_url,
            self.tool_timeout_seconds,
            self.tool_parallelism,
            self.llm_timeout.connect,
            self.llm_timeout.read,
            self.llm_timeout.write,
            self.llm_timeout.pool,
            self.llm_max_retries,
        )

    def _build_system_message(self) -> str:
        """
        Build the complete system message by combining:
        1. LLM settings system prompt (if any)
        2. chat_global_instructions (loaded fresh from GlobalSettings)
        3. Extra system instructions passed to __init__

        Returns:
            The complete system message string.
        """
        parts: List[str] = []

        # A plain completion gets ONLY its own instructions. The agent harness
        # describes tools and a coding workflow; injected into a single-shot
        # prompt it makes the model try to call tools the run never executes,
        # and the answer comes back as raw tool-call markup.
        if not self.harness:
            return self.extra_system

        # 1. LLM settings system prompt
        if self.llm_settings.system:
            parts.append(self.llm_settings.system.strip())

        # 2. chat_global_instructions (loaded fresh, not cached)
        global_instructions = _load_chat_global_instructions()
        if global_instructions:
            parts.append(global_instructions)

        # 2b. Secrets: the handle syntax plus the value-free inventory of what
        #     the runtime can actually resolve, so the model does not have to
        #     call secrets_list before its first command and never asks the user
        #     to paste a credential.
        secrets_instructions = _build_secrets_instructions(self.settings)
        if secrets_instructions:
            parts.append(secrets_instructions)

        # 3. Extra system instructions
        if self.extra_system:
            parts.append(self.extra_system)

        return "\n".join(parts).strip()

    # ── Profile tools (decided by the agent, per run) ───────────────────────────

    @staticmethod
    def _resolve_profile_names(
        config: Dict[str, Any],
        headers: Dict[str, str],
    ) -> List[str]:
        """
        Return the profiles taking part in this turn.

        The chat engine declares them in ``config["profiles"]`` or, more
        usually, in the internal ``profiles`` request header (comma separated).

        Args:
            config:  Chat configuration dict.
            headers: Request headers.

        Returns:
            Deduplicated profile names, order preserved (empty list when none).
        """
        raw = config.get("profiles")
        if raw is None:
            raw = headers.get(PROFILES_HEADER, "")

        if isinstance(raw, (list, tuple, set)):
            names = [str(name).strip() for name in raw]
        else:
            names = [name.strip() for name in str(raw or "").split(",")]

        seen: Set[str] = set()
        profile_names: List[str] = []
        for name in names:
            if name and name not in seen:
                seen.add(name)
                profile_names.append(name)
        return profile_names

    @staticmethod
    def _strip_profiles_header(headers: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """
        Return a copy of *headers* without the internal ``profiles`` header.

        Both internal headers (``profiles`` and ``orchestration``) are consumed
        by the agent and must never reach the provider. The original dict is NOT
        mutated: the chat engine reuses it for the auxiliary requests of the
        same turn (summary, chat init).

        Args:
            headers: Request headers.

        Returns:
            Headers safe to forward to the provider.
        """
        internal = {
            PROFILES_HEADER,
            EFFORT_HEADER,
            ORCHESTRATION.ORCHESTRATION_HEADER,
        }
        return {
            key: value
            for key, value in (headers or {}).items()
            if key.lower() not in internal
        }

    def _can_manage_profile_knowledge(self) -> bool:
        """
        Return True when the current user may change what profiles learn.

        The rule lives in
        :meth:`~codx.junior.security.user_management.UserSecurityManager.can_manage_profile_knowledge`
        (codx-junior admin, project admin or project knowledge admin), so the
        agent and the tool always agree.

        Returns:
            True when ``profile_learning`` may be offered to the model.
        """
        if not self.user:
            return False
        try:
            from codx.junior.security.user_management import UserSecurityManager
            return UserSecurityManager().can_manage_profile_knowledge(
                user=self.user, settings=self.settings
            )
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "SmolAgent: could not resolve profile knowledge permission for "
                "'%s': %s",
                self.user.username,
                ex,
            )
            return False

    def _profile_tools_for_run(self, profile_names: List[str]) -> List[str]:
        """
        Decide which profile tools are injected into this request.

        Profiles learn per project, but only some users may teach them:

        * ``profile_knowledge_search`` (read-only) whenever profiles take part
          in the turn,
        * ``profile_learning`` (writes rules and knowledge files) only for
          users with profile knowledge administration rights.

        Args:
            profile_names: Profiles taking part in the turn.

        Returns:
            Tool names to add to the request, empty when no profile is active.
        """
        if not profile_names:
            return []

        tools: List[str] = [PROFILE_KNOWLEDGE_TOOL]
        if self._can_manage_profile_knowledge():
            tools.append(PROFILE_LEARNING_TOOL)
        return tools

    def _load_mcp_tools(self, selected_tools: Set[str]) -> List[str]:
        """
        Load the project MCP tools granted to this turn.

        MCP discovery is project-scoped and cached by :class:`McpRegistry`. The
        method is called only when the selected grant contains an ``mcp_``
        entry, so projects without MCP servers never pay for a network call.
        The loaded entries are appended to ``self.tools``; ``SmolAgent`` then
        exposes them to the model and finds them in ``_execute_tool`` exactly
        like a built-in tool.

        Args:
            selected_tools: Model-facing tool names selected by the profiles.

        Returns:
            The names of the MCP tools actually loaded (empty on failure).
        """
        if not any(
            str(name).startswith("mcp_") for name in (selected_tools or set())
        ):
            return []
        try:
            from codx.junior.mcp.registry import McpRegistry

            existing = {
                tool["tool_json"]["function"]["name"] for tool in self.tools
            }
            entries = McpRegistry.tool_entries(self.settings, allowed=selected_tools)
            loaded: List[str] = []
            for entry in entries:
                name = entry["tool_json"]["function"]["name"]
                if name not in existing:
                    self.tools.append(entry)
                    existing.add(name)
                loaded.append(name)
            return loaded
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - a broken server is not fatal
            logger.warning("SmolAgent: cannot load MCP tools: %s", ex)
            return []

    # ── Orchestration tools (decided by the agent, per run) ───────────────────

    @staticmethod
    def _resolve_orchestration_info(
        config: Dict[str, Any],
        headers: Dict[str, str],
    ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Return the orchestration role declared by the chat engine, if any.

        The chat engine puts it in the internal ``orchestration`` header (a JSON
        object ``{run_id, step_id, role}``), which is stripped before the
        provider request. ``config["orchestration"]`` is also accepted for
        callers that build the agent directly.

        Args:
            config:  Chat configuration dict.
            headers: Request headers.

        Returns:
            The parsed info dict (``role`` is ``supervisor`` or ``worker``), or
            None when the chat does not take part in a run.
        """
        raw = config.get("orchestration")
        if raw is None:
            raw = headers.get(ORCHESTRATION.ORCHESTRATION_HEADER)

        if isinstance(raw, dict):
            info = dict(raw)
        elif raw:
            try:
                info = json.loads(str(raw))
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                logger.warning("SmolAgent: invalid orchestration header: %r", raw)
                return None
        else:
            return None

        if not isinstance(info, dict):
            return None
        role = str(info.get("role") or "").strip().lower()
        if role not in ("supervisor", "worker"):
            logger.warning("SmolAgent: unknown orchestration role: %r", role)
            return None
        info["role"] = role
        info["run_id"] = str(info.get("run_id") or "")
        info["step_id"] = str(info.get("step_id") or "")
        tools = info.get("tools")
        if isinstance(tools, (list, tuple, set)):
            info["tools"] = [str(tool).strip() for tool in tools if str(tool).strip()]
        else:
            info["tools"] = []
        return info

    @staticmethod
    def _resolve_effort_settings(
        config: Dict[str, Any],
        headers: Dict[str, str],
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Return the effort overrides declared by the active profiles.

        The chat engine resolves the ``effort`` block of the profiles taking
        part in the turn and sends it in the internal ``effort`` header (JSON).
        ``config["effort"]`` is also accepted for callers that build the agent
        directly. The values are applied on top of the tier defaults
        (``codx.junior.ai.smol.effort._apply_overrides``).

        Args:
            config:  Chat configuration dict.
            headers: Request headers.

        Returns:
            A plain dict of effort overrides (empty when none is configured).
        """
        raw = config.get("effort")
        if raw is None:
            raw = headers.get(EFFORT_HEADER)

        if isinstance(raw, dict):
            return dict(raw)
        if not raw:
            return {}
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(str(raw))
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            logger.warning("SmolAgent: invalid effort header: %r", raw)
            return {}
        return dict(parsed) if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {}

    def _orchestration_tools_for_run(
        self,
        orchestration_info: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> List[str]:
        """
        Decide which orchestration tools are injected into this request.

        * ``supervisor`` (the run main task) receives ``orchestrator`` — it plans,
          verifies and finishes the run. It does NOT receive ``delegate``: worker
          delegation is the plan itself, and the worker loop owns execution.
        * ``worker`` (a step card or a delegated subagent) receives a safe
          baseline of project tools and NEVER the orchestrator (no recursive
          planning). A profile assigned to the step can add specialized tools.

        Args:
            orchestration_info: Parsed ``orchestration`` header (or None).

        Returns:
            Tool names to add to the request.
        """
        if not orchestration_info:
            return []

        role = orchestration_info.get("role")
        if role == "supervisor":
            return [ORCHESTRATION.ORCHESTRATOR_TOOL]
        if role == "worker":
            tools = orchestration_info.get("tools") or list(
                ORCHESTRATION.DEFAULT_WORKER_TOOLS
            )
            resolved: List[str] = []
            for name in tools:
                if name and name not in resolved:
                    resolved.append(name)
            return resolved
        return []

    # ── Tool-limit policy (harness continuation) ──────────────────────────────

    def _continuation_enabled(
        self,
        config: Dict[str, Any],
        orchestration_info: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
        profile_names: List[str],
        policy: Optional[EffortPolicy] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Decide whether a tool limit CONTINUES the turn instead of stopping it.

        The decision belongs to the EFFORT POLICY
        (:func:`codx.junior.ai.smol.effort.effort_for`), not to the profile
        names: the agile tier (``codx-junior``, the default), the MAX tier and
        an orchestrated turn all continue after a tool limit with a bounded
        course correction, so a limit never dead-ends a task. A plain chat and
        an explicit ``continue_on_tool_limit=False`` stop at the limit and
        deliver the partial increment. The config key
        ``continue_on_tool_limit`` stays the highest priority override.

        Args:
            config:             Chat configuration dict.
            orchestration_info: Parsed ``orchestration`` header (or None).
            profile_names:      Profiles taking part in the turn.
            policy:             Already resolved effort policy; resolved here
                                when omitted.

        Returns:
            True when the turn must be continued after a tool limit.
        """
        explicit = config.get(CONTINUE_ON_TOOL_LIMIT_KEY)
        if explicit is not None:
            return bool(explicit)
        if policy is None:
            policy = effort_for(profile_names, orchestration_info)
        return policy.continue_on_tool_limit

    @staticmethod
    def _wall_clock_stop(
        deadline: Optional[float],
        policy: EffortPolicy,
    ) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Return the stop notice when the turn's wall-clock deadline is reached.

        The effort tier bounds how long a single turn may run. Reaching the
        deadline BREAKS the round loop (it never raises): the text and the tool
        facts already produced are still delivered, so the turn ends with a
        partial increment instead of an error.

        Args:
            deadline: Monotonic deadline (``None`` when the tier has none).
            policy:   Policy that produced the deadline (for the log/notice).

        Returns:
            The notice to append to the answer, or ``None`` when there is time
            left.
        """
        if deadline is None or time.monotonic() < deadline:
            return None
        logger.warning(
            "SmolAgent: wall-clock deadline reached after %.0fs (tier=%s); "
            "delivering the partial increment",
            policy.wall_clock_seconds,
            policy.name,
        )
        return WALL_CLOCK_EXCEEDED_MSG.format(
            tier=policy.name,
            seconds=policy.wall_clock_seconds,
        )

    def _time_pressure(
        self,
        *,
        deadline: Optional[float],
        policy: EffortPolicy,
        clock: Optional[AgileClock],
        queue: List[str],
        openai_messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        run_context: AgentRunContext,
        stage: str,
        inject: bool,
    ) -> Optional[str]:
        """
        Apply the TIME policy of the turn before continuing a round.

        Two behaviours behind one decision:

        * an ENFORCING tier (opt-in through ``stop_on_wall_clock``) returns the
          stop notice once its deadline is gone — the loop breaks, the turn is
          never raised;
        * an ADVISORY tier (agile and max by default) NEVER stops: it only asks
          the model to speed up and publishes ``AGILE_STATUS`` so the response
          metadata can be marked and the client can warn the user.

        Args:
            deadline:    Monotonic deadline (None when no clock is enforced).
            policy:      Resolved effort policy of the turn.
            clock:       Agile clock of the turn (None when not advisory).
            queue:       Pending agile notices of the turn.
            openai_messages: Conversation of THIS request (not persisted).
            run_context: Run context used to publish ``AGILE_STATUS``.
            stage:       Where the check happens (``round`` / ``tools``).
            inject:      True when it is safe to append a ``user`` message to
                         ``openai_messages`` (only right before a model
                         request: appending between an assistant tool_calls
                         message and its tool results would corrupt the
                         payload).

        Returns:
            The stop notice when the tier enforces the clock, otherwise None.
        """
        if policy.enforces_wall_clock:
            return self._wall_clock_stop(deadline, policy)
        self._agile_pressure(
            clock=clock,
            queue=queue,
            openai_messages=openai_messages if inject else None,
            run_context=run_context,
            stage=stage,
        )
        return None

    def _agile_pressure(
        self,
        *,
        clock: Optional[AgileClock],
        queue: List[str],
        openai_messages: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
        run_context: Optional[AgentRunContext] = None,
        stage: str = "round",
    ) -> Optional[AgileNudge]:
        """
        Collect the agile checkpoint reached and stress the model (never stop).

        The notice is always QUEUED for the model. When ``openai_messages`` is
        given — the safe point of the loop, right before a model request — the
        pending notices are injected as ``user`` messages of this request only:
        they are never persisted in the chat and never streamed to the user,
        who is warned through the response message metadata instead.

        Args:
            clock:           Agile clock of the turn.
            queue:           Pending notices, flushed at the next safe point.
            openai_messages: Conversation to inject the notices into, or None.
            run_context:     Run context to publish ``AGILE_STATUS`` with.
            stage:           Where the checkpoint fired (``round`` / ``tools``).

        Returns:
            The :class:`AgileNudge` produced now, or ``None``.
        """
        nudge: Optional[AgileNudge] = (
            clock.next_nudge() if clock is not None else None
        )
        if nudge is not None:
            queue.append(nudge.model_notice)
            logger.warning(
                "SmolAgent: agile checkpoint '%s' at %.0fs of %.0fs (stage=%s) "
                "— the turn is NOT stopped, asking the model to wrap up",
                nudge.level,
                nudge.elapsed_seconds,
                nudge.target_seconds,
                stage,
            )
            if run_context is not None:
                run_context.emit(
                    AgentEventType.AGILE_STATUS,
                    stage=stage,
                    level=nudge.level,
                    metadata=nudge.metadata,
                )
        if openai_messages is not None and queue:
            for notice in queue:
                openai_messages.append({"role": "user", "content": notice})
            queue.clear()
        return nudge

    def _build_tool_limit_rethink(
        self,
        openai_messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        loop_error: str,
        attempt: int,
    ) -> str:
        """
        Build the "path rethink" notice injected when a tool limit is reached.

        The notice is deterministic (no AI request and no extra cost): it
        explains that the guardrail tripped, hands back every fact the tools
        already produced so nothing must be re-discovered, and forces a path
        change — fewer calls, act on what is known, or ask the user for the
        exact decision that is missing.

        Args:
            openai_messages: Current OpenAI-format conversation (this run only).
            loop_error:      The LoopGuard message that tripped.
            attempt:         Continuation number (1-based).

        Returns:
            The notice content, injected as a user message of THIS turn only.
        """
        facts = self._tool_usage_fallback(self._collect_tool_usage(openai_messages))
        facts = (facts or "").strip()
        if len(facts) > TOOL_LIMIT_FACTS_MAX_CHARS:
            facts = facts[:TOOL_LIMIT_FACTS_MAX_CHARS].rstrip() + "\n… (more facts omitted)"
        return TOOL_LIMIT_RETHINK_TEMPLATE.format(
            loop_error=loop_error,
            facts=facts or "(no tool returned data yet)",
            attempt=attempt,
            attempts=TOOL_LIMIT_CONTINUATIONS,
            max_calls=TOOL_LIMIT_CONTINUATION_MAX_TOOL_CALLS,
        )

    # ── Public API ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def chat(
        self,
        messages: List[Union[AIMessage, HumanMessage]],
        config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> AgentRunResult:
        """
        Run a streaming chat completion with iterative multi-step tool support.

        The whole run is wrapped in :meth:`AgentRunContext.run`, which emits
        ``RUN_START`` / ``RUN_END`` / ``RUN_ERROR`` / ``RUN_CANCELLED`` events
        with an analytics summary attached.

        Tool results are cached within this conversation to avoid re-execution
        if the model requests the same tool with identical arguments.

        Loop limits are handled gracefully: instead of raising, the run is
        continued for a harness task (the facts already collected are handed
        back with a "rethink the path" instruction and a smaller budget, see
        :meth:`_build_tool_limit_rethink`), and only then stopped with a
        summary of the tools used appended to the assistant answer (see
        :meth:`_summarize_tool_usage`). This keeps the work in the persisted
        message so the next iteration can continue without repeating the same
        tools.

        Cost limits are handled gracefully too: every round's cost (plus any
        cost reported by tools via :attr:`ToolResponse.cost`) is accumulated and
        returned in the typed :class:`AgentRunResult`. Once the chat reaches
        ``Chat.estimation_cost``, the run stops before executing further tools so
        the chat never exceeds its budget.

        Provider errors (connection refused, DNS, timeout, TLS, bad request,
        ...) are logged verbosely with a traceback and mirrored to the client
        before being re-raised (see :meth:`_log_ai_error`).

        Message Structure
        The response always appends a single final answer AIMessage containing
        the model's own text. Tool output is delivered separately as a
        collapsible message property (``ToolEvent.output``) instead of being
        merged into the content, so the client can decide how to render it.

        Args:
            messages: Conversation history as LangChain message objects.
            config:   Optional dict with keys: ``tools``, ``profiles``,
                      ``chat_id``, ``cancellation_token``, ``headers``,
                      ``callbacks``, ``run_context`` (an
                      :class:`AgentRunContext`), ``event_listeners`` (list of
                      event callables), ``current_chat`` (the Chat object for
                      context), and ``vision_content`` (optional vision API
                      content blocks).

        Returns:
            The typed :class:`AgentRunResult` for this run. Its ``messages``
            attribute contains the updated conversation (with the final
            assistant reply appended); ``cost`` carries the cost breakdown.

        Raises:
            CancelledError: If the request is cancelled by the caller.
        """
        config = config or {}
        self._preflight_limit_check()

        run_context = self._resolve_run_context(config)
        result: Optional[AgentRunResult] = None

        # run_context.run() emits RUN_* lifecycle events. It swallows
        # AgentCancelled (emitting RUN_CANCELLED), so we translate the
        # cancelled state back to the legacy CancelledError afterwards.
        with run_context.run():
            result = await self._run_chat_loop(messages, config, run_context)

        if run_context.token.cancelled or result is None:
            raise CancelledError(CANCELLED_MESSAGE)
        return result

    def _resolve_loop_limits(self, policy: EffortPolicy) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """
        Return the loop budget of the resolved effort policy.

        Effort is the ONLY source of the round/tool budget: the active profile
        (``codx-junior``/``codx-junior-max`` or a project profile with an
        ``effort`` block) supplies the values, and the tier constants are the
        fallback. Model/provider settings no longer carry agent budgets, so
        there is no second precedence ladder to reason about.

        Args:
            policy: Effort policy of the turn (already overridden by the
                    active profile's ``effort`` block).

        Returns:
            ``(max_iterations, max_tool_calls)`` for the LoopGuard.
        """
        return policy.max_iterations, policy.max_tool_calls

    # ── Chat loop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def _run_chat_loop(
        self,
        messages: List[Union[AIMessage, HumanMessage]],
        config: Dict[str, Any],
        run_context: AgentRunContext,
    ) -> AgentRunResult:
        """
        Execute the iterative streaming/tool loop for one conversation.

        Response accumulation strategy:
        - ``thinking_content``: Accumulates the model's OWN text (reasoning)
          produced during tool-calling rounds. Streamed live to the client via
          send_callback and included in the final AIMessage. Tool output is NOT
          added here: dual-response tool ``user_response`` values are emitted on
          the ``TOOL_END`` event and attached to the response message as a
          collapsible property (``ToolEvent.output``).
        - ``final_answer_content``: Accumulates LLM text during the final
          round (after the model stops making tool calls).

        Message generation:
        - Always emits exactly one AIMessage containing thinking_content and
          final_answer_content. Since tool output is no longer merged into the
          content, the message may legitimately be empty (a run that only
          executed tools); the assistant message is still appended so callers
          can rely on ``messages[-1]``. All run information (cost, usage, tool
          summaries) is returned in the typed :class:`AgentRunResult`.

        Tool caching:
        - Identical tool calls (same name + args) are cached per conversation.
        - Cached results bypass LoopGuard checks (don't count towards limits).
        - Cached tool results are only reused for the model message; they do NOT
          re-emit tool output (the first execution already delivered it).

        Loop limits:
        - A harness turn (orchestration worker/supervisor, delegated subagent or
          the harness profile) that reaches a tool limit is CONTINUED: the
          facts already collected are injected back with a "rethink the path"
          instruction and the guard is renewed with a smaller budget.
        - When the continuations are exhausted (or the turn is a plain chat),
          LoopGuard stops the loop gracefully (no exception propagates) and a
          summary of the tools used is appended to ``thinking_content`` so it
          is streamed to the user and persisted in the final answer.

        Cost limits:
        - Every round is priced in cxjcoins from provider usage + model prices
          and accumulated into the chat total. When the chat reaches its
          ``estimation_cost``, the loop is broken gracefully (before running
          more tools) and a notice is appended to the answer.

        Args:
            messages:    Conversation history as LangChain message objects.
            config:      Chat configuration dict (see :meth:`chat`).
            run_context: Unified runtime context for this run.

        Returns:
            The typed :class:`AgentRunResult` for this run.

        Raises:
            AgentCancelled: If cancellation is requested mid-run.
        """
        chat_id: Optional[str] = config.get("chat_id")
        cancellation_token: Optional[CancellationToken] = config.get(
            "cancellation_token"
        )
        headers: Dict[str, str] = config.get("headers", {})
        # Profiles taking part in this turn, declared by the chat engine in an
        # internal header (never forwarded to the provider). The AGENT — not the
        # profile definition — decides which profile tools are injected.
        profile_names: List[str] = self._resolve_profile_names(config, headers)
        orchestration_info = self._resolve_orchestration_info(config, headers)
        provider_headers: Dict[str, str] = self._strip_profiles_header(headers)
        session_id: Optional[str] = headers.get("session_id")
        tags: str = self._build_tags(headers)

        # Inject session context into settings for tools that need it
        current_chat = config.get("current_chat")
        if self.session and current_chat:
            self.settings._active_session = self.session
            self.session._current_chat = current_chat
        # Expose the cancellation token to tools that spawn nested work (the
        # `delegate` tool cancels its subagents when the parent turn is
        # cancelled). Best effort: settings is a plain model.
        try:
            self.settings._active_cancellation_token = cancellation_token
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            pass

        send_callback = self._make_callback_sender(config.get("callbacks"))
        kwargs = self._build_request_kwargs(
            config.get("tools", []),
            profile_names=profile_names,
            orchestration_info=orchestration_info,
        )
        # ── Effort policy: the ONLY source of the turn budget ────────────────
        # The tier comes from the profile names (codx.junior.ai.smol.effort):
        # ``codx-junior`` is agile (ADVISORY clock) and ``codx-junior-max`` has
        # the heavier defaults. The active profiles may carry an ``effort``
        # block (sent by the chat engine in the internal header) that overrides
        # those defaults, so a project can tune the budget without touching
        # model/provider settings. Neither tier can dead-end a task: a reached
        # limit grants the bounded course correction below. The config key
        # ``continue_on_tool_limit`` remains the highest priority override.
        effort_settings = self._resolve_effort_settings(config, headers)
        effort_policy: EffortPolicy = effort_for(
            profile_names,
            orchestration_info,
            explicit=(
                None
                if config.get(CONTINUE_ON_TOOL_LIMIT_KEY) is None
                else bool(config.get(CONTINUE_ON_TOOL_LIMIT_KEY))
            ),
            settings=effort_settings,
        )
        logger.info(
            "SmolAgent: effort tier=%s max_iterations=%d max_tool_calls=%d "
            "continuations=%d wall_clock_s=%.0f validation=%s "
            "profile_overrides=%s",
            effort_policy.name,
            effort_policy.max_iterations,
            effort_policy.max_tool_calls,
            effort_policy.continuations,
            effort_policy.wall_clock_seconds,
            effort_policy.validation,
            sorted(effort_settings) if effort_settings else "none",
        )

        # ── Agile clock: pressure the model, never kill the turn ─────────────
        # The agile tier promises an increment in ``AGILE_TARGET_SECONDS`` (20
        # minutes). Its clock is ADVISORY: every checkpoint injects a
        # deterministic "hurry up" notice into the model conversation and
        # publishes ``AGILE_STATUS`` so the response metadata can be marked and
        # the client can warn the user. The turn is NEVER broken by the clock —
        # only the human stops it. MAX has the same advisory behaviour with a
        # longer target; a caller may opt into an ENFORCED clock through the
        # effort policy (nothing enables it by default).
        agile_clock: Optional[AgileClock] = agile_clock_for(
            effort_policy, started_at=time.monotonic()
        )
        # Final agile state stamped on the response message (None when the tier
        # has no advisory target).
        agile_metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
        # Agile notices waiting for the next SAFE injection point (right before
        # a model request). They are never persisted in the chat.
        agile_notices: List[str] = []
        if agile_clock is not None:
            logger.info(
                "SmolAgent: advisory clock active (mode=%s target=%.0fs, "
                "checkpoints=%s)",
                agile_clock.mode,
                agile_clock.target_seconds,
                agile_clock.checkpoints,
            )

        # Build system message dynamically on each chat (fresh global
        # instructions). An agile turn is TOLD it is on the clock: the tier is a
        # runtime policy, but a model that does not know it is being timed does
        # not hurry up.
        system_message = self._build_system_message()
        # Only the agile tier gets the AGILE MODE prompt section: the max tier
        # has its own profile instructions and a much longer target.
        if agile_clock is not None and effort_policy.name == "agile":
            system_message += agile_system_section(agile_clock.target_seconds)
        openai_messages = to_openai_messages(messages, system=system_message)

        # Initialize LoopGuard from the EFFORT POLICY. The active profile's
        # ``effort`` block (codx-junior / codx-junior-max or a project profile)
        # already overrode the tier defaults; model/provider no longer carry an
        # agent budget. These limits are enforced on every tool round to prevent
        # runaway execution or breadth violations.
        # NOTE: the policy also carries ``max_tool_rounds``; LoopGuard has no
        # equivalent parameter yet (follow-up, not invented here).
        loop_max_iterations, loop_max_tool_calls = self._resolve_loop_limits(
            effort_policy
        )
        logger.info(
            "SmolAgent: loop limits max_iterations=%s max_tool_calls=%s "
            "(tier=%s)",
            loop_max_iterations,
            loop_max_tool_calls,
            effort_policy.name,
        )
        loop_guard = LoopGuard(
            max_iterations=loop_max_iterations,
            max_tool_calls=loop_max_tool_calls,
        )

        # Initialize tool cache for this conversation.
        # Cached results bypass LoopGuard checks and don't count towards limits.
        tool_cache = ToolCache()

        # ── Tool-limit continuation (decided by the effort policy) ────────────
        # The tool limits are a GUARDRAIL against rabbit holes, not a stop
        # condition for MAX work: a ``codx-junior-max`` turn that runs out of
        # tool budget is CONTINUED in the same turn (the facts it already
        # collected + a smaller budget) so the run resolves itself instead of
        # dying. Agile (``codx-junior``, the default) has ``continuations=0`` and
        # plain chats keep the old behaviour: they stop at the limit and deliver
        # the partial increment.
        continue_on_tool_limit: bool = self._continuation_enabled(
            config=config,
            orchestration_info=orchestration_info,
            profile_names=profile_names,
            policy=effort_policy,
        )
        # Course corrections granted by the tier. Both agile and MAX grant them:
        # a tool limit must never dead-end a task. Only a plain chat (or an
        # explicit ``continue_on_tool_limit=False``) stops at the limit.
        tool_limit_continuations_max: int = max(
            0, int(effort_policy.continuations or 0)
        )
        tool_limit_continuations: int = 0
        tool_limit_note: str = ""

        # Chat cost budget: seed the accumulated chat cost from Chat.cost, the
        # deletion-safe accumulator maintained by ChatManager. Falling back to
        # summing the message costs keeps this working for chats persisted
        # before the accumulator existed.
        chat_cost: float = self._accumulated_chat_cost(current_chat)
        # Cost of THIS run (this SmolAgent iteration).
        iteration_cost: float = 0.0

        # Typed run accumulators (replace the previous additional_kwargs contract).
        # They feed the returned AgentRunResult.cost breakdown.
        total_input_tokens: int = 0
        total_output_tokens: int = 0
        total_input_cost: float = 0.0
        total_output_cost: float = 0.0
        total_tool_cost: float = 0.0
        tool_cost_by_name: Dict[str, float] = {}

        request_start = time.monotonic()

        # Wall-clock deadline ENFORCED by the effort tier (opt-in only: no
        # built-in tier enables it). When it is set the round loop breaks
        # instead of raising, so the partial increment survives. The normal
        # path is the ADVISORY clock handled above.
        wall_clock_deadline: Optional[float] = (
            request_start + effort_policy.wall_clock_seconds
            if effort_policy.enforces_wall_clock
            else None
        )

        # Track whether any tools were used in this conversation.
        tools_were_used: bool = False

        # thinking_content: accumulates the model's OWN text (reasoning) during
        # tool-calling rounds. Streamed live to client AND included in the final
